The TVK, led by actor Vijay, has emerged as a potential disruptor, offering a share of power to voters disillusioned with established parties. While the DMK faces internal challenges in seat-sharing negotiations with allies like the Congress and CPI(M), the AIADMK is attempting to solidify its alliance with the BJP despite criticism from within. The outcome will likely hinge on voter sentiment and the effectiveness of campaign strategies by both major players.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls: Gandhi siblings recast Wayanad politics, but local fault lines persist - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The 2021 Kerala Assembly election saw the **Gandhi** siblings, Rahul and Priyanka, secure victories in Wayanad.  While Rahul Gandhi won the Lok Sabha seat with a significant margin in both 2019 and 2024, his sister Priyanka's victory in a byelection further solidified the family's influence. The election results were influenced by regional issues such as welfare schemes, tribal development, and human-wildlife conflict.  The **LDF** retained Mananthavady while the **UDF** capitalized on agrarian distress to win Kalpetta and Sulthan Bathery.

recent_articles.title: A game of four - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Tamil Nadu political landscape is set for a lively election, with the DMK and AIADMK facing challenges from new entrants like the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). The DMK, seeking to maintain its dominance, faces internal dissent within its alliance partners while the AIADMK seeks to reclaim lost ground.  The TVK's emergence as a potential spoiler has added complexity to an already intricate political chessboard.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Polls 2026: Sudheer Karamana to be LDF Independent candidate in Thiruvanananthapuram - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Independent** actor Sudheer Karamana was chosen as the **Left Democratic Front (LDF)** candidate for the Thiruvananthapuram constituency.  The LDF, after the disqualification of sitting MLA Antony Raju from the **Janadhipathya Kerala Congress (JKC),** decided to field Mr. Karamana. The decision comes after a pending decision on the seat allocation and the subsequent selection of Mr. Sameer from Tanur as a replacement for Mr. Abdurahiman, who was shifted to Tirur.

recent_articles.title: Will Vadakara witness consolidation of anti-CPI(M) votes again? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming Vadakara Assembly election will see the **CPI(M)** and its socialist allies facing a challenge from the **United Democratic Front (UDF)**, which has benefited from anti-**CPI(M)** sentiment fueled by splits within the party. The **RMP**, led by T.P. Chandrasekharan, has gained traction in recent years, securing votes through alliances with the UDF and support from influential groups like the **Indian Union Muslim League**.  The LDF, fielding a candidate who previously held local office positions, seeks to retain its stronghold while the NDA aims for increased representation.

recent_articles.title: Kerala polls: 4 LDF Ministers declare assets of ₹2 crore each - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Several **LDF** ministers in Kerala declared assets exceeding ₹1.94 crore to ₹2.29 crore in their nomination papers ahead of the April 9 Assembly elections.  **K.N. Balagopal, V. Sivankutty, R. Bindu**, and **Roshy Augustine** reported substantial wealth while **PWD Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas** declared assets worth ₹40 lakh and his wife, **Veena T**, a daughter of **Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan**, has assets exceeding ₹2 crore.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Polls 2026: P.K. Sasi to contest as UDF-backed Independent in Ottappalam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **P.K. Sasi**, a former **CPI(M)** leader, will contest the Ottapalam Assembly seat as an Independent candidate after being denied the Congress symbol. The **UDF** is supporting him following the Congress's decision to withhold the 'hand' symbol due to local party leader objections. Mr. Sasi was expelled from the **CPI(M)** for publicly criticizing its leadership and plans to expose "wrongdoers" before the public.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly polls 2026: 537 nomination papers filed till 7.30 p.m. on Saturday - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Election officials** in Kerala received a high volume of nomination papers for the upcoming Assembly elections on Saturday, with over 500 filed by the end of the day.  Prominent candidates from various political parties, including **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan**, **K.N. Balagopal**, and **Ramesh Chennithala**, submitted their papers. The scrutiny of these nominations will begin on Tuesday, March 24th, with a withdrawal deadline set for March 26th.

recent_articles.title: P.K. Sasi to contest as UDF-backed Independent in Ottappalam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **P.K. Sasi**, an expelled **CPI(M)** leader, will contest the Ottapalam Assembly seat as an Independent candidate after the **Congress** refused to allot him its 'hand' symbol. The UDF, which initially planned to field Mr. Sasi on the Congress symbol, decided to support his independent candidacy following objections from local party leaders.  Mr. Sasi was recently expelled from the **CPI(M)** for criticizing its leadership and has since vowed to expose "wrongdoers" within the party.

recent_articles.title: Sudheer Karamana to be LDF Independent candidate at Thiruvanananthapuram - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Independent** actor Sudheer Karamana was chosen as the **Left Democratic Front (LDF)** candidate for the Thiruvananthapuram constituency. The decision came after the **Janadhipathya Kerala Congress (JKC)**, an LDF ally, failed to field a replacement for their disqualified MLA, Antony Raju.  Karamana will face off against candidates from the Communist Marxist Party (CMP), United Democratic Front (UDF), and BJP.

recent_articles.title: Kerala Assembly Elections 2026: Segments under Vadakara LS seat could see some keen contests - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming elections in the Vadakara Lok Sabha constituency are expected to be closely contested, with **the Left Democratic Front (LDF)** holding an advantage in several Assembly segments.  **K.P. Kunhammad Kutty** of the CPI(M) won Kuttiyadi and Nadapuram in 2016 and 2021 respectively, while **E.K. Vijayan** of the CPI won in Nadapuram in 2016 and 2021. The UDF is hoping to capitalize on its recent local body election success and the popularity of **Shafi Parambil**, the Vadakara MP, as well as the organizational strength of the IUML and RMPI in these areas.  The LDF is relying on the support of traditional voters and the state government's development initiatives.

recent_articles.title: Kerala polls: Ex-CPI(M) Minister G. Sudhakaran files papers as ‘people’s Independent’ in Ambalappuzha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **G. Sudhakaran**, a former CPI(M) minister, filed his nomination as an independent candidate in the Ambalappuzha Assembly constituency in Kerala.  Sudhakaran's move has sparked a political battle with his one-time protege **H. Salam** of the CPI(M). The UDF, eager to challenge the LDF in its home turf, has offered Sudhakaran their support. The CPI(M) remains confident about winning despite Sudhakaran's defection and the subsequent rebellion within the Congress.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu Assembly election: CPI(M) meeting to decide on seat-sharing with DMK - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Communist Party of India (Marxist)** (CPI(M)) is set to decide on seat-sharing with the **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam** (DMK) at its State committee meeting in Chennai.  **M.A. Baby**, the CPI(M)'s general secretary, is attending the meeting where the party will discuss their demand for at least six seats contested in the previous Assembly election, a number that **DMK** is unwilling to concede. The two parties have already held three rounds of talks but haven't reached an agreement.

recent_articles.title: Kerala CM blames successive Congress, BJP governments at Centre for India’s cooking gas crisis - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Pinarayi Vijayan**, Kerala Chief Minister, blamed **Congress** and **BJP** governments at the Centre for the ongoing cooking gas scarcity. He argued that their decisions to reject the India-Iran gas pipeline in 2006 and subsequent policies favoring private sector interests have contributed to the crisis.  **Vijayan** accused both parties of overlooking the economic fallout, including job losses and inflation, while failing to increase LNG production or secure sufficient crude oil reserves. He stated that these failures have exacerbated the cost-of-living crisis in the country.
